_readme: Museum spatial-design principles extracted from literature for the endless museum (2026-07-21). Provenance: literature-unverified — the deep-research verifier panels died on a usage limit, so each claim carries its source but zero adversarial votes (P-10: these PROPOSE, never bind; a ruling or our own measurement outranks them). maps_to ties each principle to the pipeline concept it parameterizes.

vitruvian._note: Palle 2026-07-21: 'imagine a Vitruvian space' — the corridor proportioned from the walking, seeing body. These constants are MEASURED in our own pipeline (provenance: code), and the corridor's dimensions are their radii: width 13-17 brackets 2 x promise (16 m) — the corridor width IS the promise diameter.

principles.claim: Viewing distance scales linearly with artwork size: distance ~ 1.4 m + 0.21 m per m2 of canvas (r2=0.93); mean 1.75 m, range 1.49-2.12 m.
principles.maps_to: gaze_ride size oracle; em-square viewing contract; wing offset from walk path

principles.claim: Initial viewing of an artwork averages 33.9 s (median 25.1); counting return visits, total viewing averages 50.5 s (median 43.0).
principles.number: 33.9 s first look, 50.5 s with returns

principles.claim: In free-plan galleries 55.3% of visitors return to an already-viewed artwork (up to six times); forced single paths forfeit the return visit.
principles.maps_to: cost of the endless-runner form; loop templates and backtrack scoring

principles.claim: Room occupancy in the Tate correlates with visual shallowness (visibility-graph mean path length, R2=0.63); plain metric centrality predicts nothing. Seeing, not distance, drives flow. Validated on a 1 m analysis grid.
principles.maps_to: gaze_ride IS a visibility instrument; 1 cell = 1 m is the validated resolution

principles.claim: Minimum route width 1525 mm for two-way flow, and even one-way routes should be 1525 mm so a visitor can STOP TO LOOK without blocking movement; passing spaces every <=61 m on narrower routes.
principles.number: 1.5 m lanes; stop-and-look is a width requirement
principles.maps_to: corridor width budget: 2 lanes + 2 stop pockets + axis fits in 13-17 cells

principles.claim: Stopping to inspect requires a clear pocket ~760 x 1220 mm per viewing side of a display, overlapping the route.
principles.maps_to: one free cell in front of every wing artifact — a placement contract

principles.claim: Across 34 tracked exhibitions visitors averaged ~13 minutes and stopped at ~29% of exhibits; 'diligent visitors' (>=51% of stops) benchmark at 25%.
principles.maps_to: coverage target honesty: a map must read when hero + 2 are consumed

principles.claim: Attention declines after 30-45 minutes (museum fatigue); dwell drops ~34% through a visit; object satiation — sameness dulls attention.
principles.maps_to: sequence length (7-10 maps x 3-5 min); register alternation; chamber as mid-sequence rest (2026-07-19 chamber rule)

principles.claim: Visitors take the shortest route to the first visible exit (Melton). Museums fight it; the composed corridor aligns hero and exit on one axis so the pull toward the exit IS the pull through the promise.
principles.maps_to: P-1 axis discipline; close register (hero last, on axis)

principles.claim: Curators use two opposite hero placements: bury the masterpiece in the deepest dead-end to pull visitors through everything (Sainsbury Wing), or put it in the most integrated space to catch existing flow (Pompidou 5).
principles.maps_to: two template families: deep-hero (close register) vs integrated-hero (turn/chamber)

principles.claim: Long synchronized axes with uniform isovists aid orientation but DIMINISH the visual impact of individual works — promising from afar spends the work's surprise.
principles.maps_to: the Spectacle question; when to break axis discipline (worn heroes, thresholds)

principles.claim: Pacing devices slow walking into looking: at Castelvecchio long vistas are end-stopped by blank walls; thresholds and decompression rooms reset attention between dense rooms.
principles.maps_to: register rhythm arrival/promenade/close; temporal void as rest beat (P-4)
